candidate_relations.reason: Fungal infection is the correct kingdom-level parent missing Histoplasma and primary oral scope.
Mucormycosis shows ribbon-like hyphae, not intracellular yeasts with halos.
Oral lichen planus is an immune-mediated white reticular disease, not a yeast-filled ulcer.
Blastomyces yeasts are large broad-based budding forms, a different dimorphic fungus.
Sporotrichosis is typically lymphocutaneous, not an isolated tongue ulcer with halo yeasts.
A diabetic tongue ulcer would not contain intracellular yeasts highlighted by GMS/PAS.
Paracoccidioidomycosis (mariner’s-wheel yeasts) is geographically and morphologically a different dimorphic fungus.
Oral tuberculosis is a mycobacterial ulcer, not GMS-positive yeasts.
Histoplasma infection identifies the organism but omits the primary oral localization.
Mucocutaneous leishmaniasis shows amastigotes, not GMS-positive halo yeasts.
There was no trauma history; a chronic traumatic ulcer would not contain yeasts.
Chronic granulomatous disease is a primary immunodeficiency, not the tongue-ulcer diagnosis.
Histoplasmosis is the correct disease family but omits the primary oral qualifier required by the reference.
Oral leukoplakia is a white plaque, not an ulcer packed with yeasts.

case_quality_flags: Intracellular halo yeasts on GMS/PAS in an isolated tongue ulcer of an HIV-negative patient support primary oral histoplasmosis; culture was negative, which does not exclude the diagnosis.
